newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan army chief says armed bands more active.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan army chief says armed bands more active.

text.p: Nicaragua's army chief said on Tuesday heavily armed bands operating in Nicaragua have become more active since the Oct. 20 elections.
"There has been a mobilisation of the major armed bands since Oct. 20," Gen. Joaquin Cuadra told reporters.
Such bands, many armed with assault rifles and other military weaponry left over from Nicaragua's civil war of the 1980s, have become a permanent fixture in the rural mountains.

Cuadra said the number of armed bands has increased and attributed this to their desire to have a better bargaining position in demobilization talks with the new government that will take power on Jan. 10.

Officials from right-wing President-elect Arnoldo Aleman's Liberal Alliance have been in contact with leaders of these armed groups and publicly speculated of a major demobilization once the Liberals come to power.
Aleman's Liberal Alliance includes members of the former U.S.-backed Contra rebels.

Cuadra did not give details on the number of groups active or the number of attacks, but the army has previously said about 400 armed men belonging to 35 bands continue to operate in remote areas of northern and central Nicaragua.

Many are loose descendants of the former right-wing Contra rebels or members of the left-wing Sandinista army who laid down their arms in the 1990 peace agreement, but later re-armed, unhappy with the demobilization process. Others are considered common criminals.
